verdict.rationale: The design covers all six cc-layer work items from synthesis §9.1, honors FR-5 (zero ADRs authored, 9 Q-CC-N items deferred), preserves the C-0445 grep-verified zero-mcp__ invariant for 29 of 36 agents, and conforms to the trifecta structural conventions extracted in synthesis §6. The four conditions are all 'Composer-bound, not author-bound' — they cannot be resolved by the design-cc agent itself per FR-5, and the design surfaces them correctly. No critical issues; one important issue (I-DR-001 inventory-count mismatch) and four recommended improvements.

issues.location: Inventory of CC primitives (table row 1) + `.mcp.json` design (note on codebase-memory-mcp at line 176) + AC-CC-1 (line 499) + Q-CC-6 (line 544)
issues.description: The design includes 8 servers in .mcp.json (the 7 PRD-named primaries PLUS codebase-memory-mcp as the ADR-0018 fallback). The PRD v3 explicitly closes the named-server list at seven. AC-CC-1 states 'shall list exactly the seven named servers ... plus codebase-memory-mcp ... as connected' which surfaces the contradiction inline. Q-CC-6 names the conflict and recommends interpretation (a) — fallback is implicit, not the eighth primary — but the AC text still couples the count promise to the fallback. As written, an audit run against AC-CC-1 will either flag the 8th entry as drift OR have to special-case codebase-memory-mcp; either path needs a recorded convention.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) update AC-CC-1 to explicitly say '7 named primaries + 1 documented fallback (codebase-memory-mcp per ADR-0018) = 8 mcpServers entries total' and have OP-2 / OP-3 in auditing-mcp special-case codebase-memory-mcp by name; or (b) defer the codebase-memory-mcp .mcp.json registration to a follow-up feature and document the resulting fallback unavailability. Composer should record the chosen convention in the UI-15 ADR (synthesis §7 risk 1) or a separate one-paragraph ADR-amendment to ADR-0018.

issues.location: Subagent patterns — per-agent allowlist updates (table row 7, line 216)
issues.description: Row 7 of the per-agent allowlist table is 'TBD per D-13 narrowing' with no concrete agent list. The downstream plan-author cannot author per-agent edits for Serena consumers without this list. Q-CC-3 surfaces the question correctly but the design subsection itself leaves the consumer-mapping table incomplete on 1 of 7 rows.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) add a provisional list to the table (e.g., 'review-architecture-auditor + design-cc; subject to Composer confirmation in Q-CC-3') so the table is concrete-default-overridable, or (b) explicitly state in the table cell that 'Serena row finalization blocks plan-authoring; design-cc returns to Composer before plan-author runs.' The current 'TBD' is correct but underspecified about the resolution mechanism.

issues.description: The gitnexus entry's args use `git+https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus@<PIN_TAG>` — but codebase-analysis.json line 221 records the canonical source as 'abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus' AND synthesis D-11 says 'exact tag per ADR-0007 v2.2.0'. The `<PIN_TAG>` placeholder is correct (pin determined at install time, per D-11 verify-at-execution discipline), but the surrounding prose at line 176 also uses '<TBD-per-ADR-0007-v2.2.0>' for codebase-memory-mcp's command — these two placeholder conventions should be unified.
issues.suggestion: Use a single placeholder convention across all TBD pins (e.g., always `<PIN_TBD>` or always `<TBD-per-ADR-NNNN>`) and add a 1-line note above the .mcp.json sketch saying 'placeholders of the form `<...>` are resolved at plan-author time per D-11.' Minor consistency win for the downstream plan-author who will template-fill these.

issues.location: `mcp-events.jsonl` schema (UI-15 contract) — 'What the file is NOT' subsection (line 339-343)
issues.description: The schema correctly enumerates 3 event types (primary_degraded, readiness_probe, structured_failure) but does not specify how the file is BOOTSTRAPPED — i.e., what state the file is in before postCreate runs. Without bootstrap semantics, OP-5 (lifecycle health-check completeness, line 480) cannot tell 'postStart never ran' from 'postStart ran and produced no events.' This matters for the AC-FR-8-c 'stale beyond a threshold' clause in PRD.
issues.suggestion: Add a single line to the schema section: 'On postCreate, the file is created (touch) if absent; postStart appends 7 readiness_probe records on every container start. An absent file or zero records after postStart indicates a layer-zero failure (the hook did not run) and is itself an OP-5 BLOCKER.' This unblocks the auditing-mcp OP-5 rule definition and gives plan-author a concrete contract.

issues.description: Two pedagogical_sections entries are declared (auth-and-redaction.md and lifecycle-hooks.md), each with brief justifications. The justifications are correct in shape but could be tightened — e.g., 'Names anti-patterns ... that the auditor would otherwise flag as anti-pattern occurrences' could be more specific about WHICH auditor rule. Given KB-documentation-criteria/references/pedagogical-marker-justification-spec.md (substance-keyword requirement), the current text passes the rules but is more generic than the KB-github-actions-platform 8 entries that codebase-analysis flags as the richest set.
issues.suggestion: When authoring (this is an outline, not the final SKILL.md), aim for justifications that explicitly name (a) the specific anti-pattern (e.g., 'E-0094 argv-leakage'), (b) which auditing-mcp rule would flag it (e.g., 'OP-10'), and (c) why the reference legitimately names it (e.g., 'reference legitimately documents anti-pattern as guidance, not as project occurrence'). This is a forward-quality nudge; the outline is fine for design-stage review.

issues.description: The .mcp.json sketch uses ```jsonc as the language fence. Per KB-general-coding-principles dimension 9 (language matches project): the project's existing examples (`KB-cc-platform/assets/templates/mcp-config.json.example` per codebase-analysis) use straight `.json` extension. JSONC (JSON-with-comments) is appropriate for sketches with prose comments BUT introduces a divergence from the project's existing template extension. Acceptable as a design-time sample with comments, but the FINAL artifact (KB-mcp-platform/assets/templates/.mcp.json.example) should use `.json` and move comments to surrounding prose, OR the project should standardize on JSONC for its MCP templates.
issues.suggestion: Add a one-line note in the sketch caption: 'rendered as jsonc here for inline comments; final template is .json with comments moved to surrounding prose in KB-mcp-platform.' This addresses KB-general-coding-principles dimension 9 (language matches project) and prevents the plan-author from accidentally committing a .jsonc file when the project convention is .json.
